rapids.name: Upper Goat Creek Rapid

rapids.name: Lower Goat Creek Rapid

history: Debris flows from side creeks have rebuilt rapids more than once, including Bernard Creek in 2003, the Tappan rapids in 2008 and Velvet Falls and Hells Half Mile in 2023. Look before you run, even rapids you know.
Earthquake Rock Rapid was formed by rockfall during the 1983 Borah Peak earthquake.
Whitie Cox, a miner who died in 1954, is buried at the camp that bears his name.

rules.d: The permit holder's government photo ID and the printed, signed permit. Boats are inspected at Boundary Creek and Indian Creek.
A metal fire pan of at least 144 square inches with sides at least 3 inches high (kayakers 2 inches). Required even if you build no fire. An unmodified garbage-can lid does not count.

A fire blanket in good condition large enough to catch embers (required since 2023), and a metal or hard plastic ash container with a sealable lid. Bags and dry bags are not acceptable. Kayakers need 300 cubic inches.
A porta-potty system sized for all human and pet waste. Plan about 1 lb per person per day. Only toilet paper and solid waste go in; no wipes, tampons or ash. Add water before the take-out.
A mesh strainer fine enough for coffee grounds, a shovel (folding is fine; kayakers may use a paddle) and a bucket (a cooking pot will do).
An Idaho AIS sticker on each boat (inflatable non-motorized craft under 10 ft are exempt). Boats must be clean, drained and dry on arrival and are inspected.
Camp only in the camps listed on your permit, with the whole group together. An assigned camp is not exclusive; expect to share it, especially at hot springs and airstrips.
A group may be assigned at most one hot spring camp, and it is not guaranteed.
During the control season, only one night per trip below Big Creek (mile 77.9). Layovers are limited and approved case by case.
Do not stay in or visit assigned camps after 7 p.m. Keep noise down.
Fires only in the fire pan, raised on rocks with a layer of sand or dirt. Gather only dead and down wood. Dampen ashes in the ash container and pack them out. Carry charcoal in case of restrictions.
The river runs through the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness. Drones, motors and mechanical transport are not allowed. Use a manual pump at Indian Creek.
Put food and drink away after meals and keep containers closed. Do not feed wildlife.
Dogs must be leashed at guard stations, launches and take-outs. Pack out dog waste.
Do not touch pictographs or collect artifacts.
Avoid disturbing salmon nests in the main river and tributaries, especially in late summer and fall.
A valid Idaho fishing license is required and is not sold at the launches. Fishing is mostly catch and release with artificial flies or lures and a single barbless hook. Live bait is prohibited.

landmarks.name: Cougar Creek Ranch

landmarks.name: Flying B Ranch

landmarks.name: Parrot Cabin

landmarks.name: Salmon River confluence

landmarks.name: Cache Bar
landmarks.desc: The standard take-out with paved ramps. Heavy traffic 9 to 11 a.m. from mid-June to mid-August.

permit.status: Required year-round · lottery May 28 to Sept 3

items.d: Applications for control-season dates (May 28 to September 3) are taken on Recreation.gov from December 1 to January 31. Results are emailed February 14, and winners must confirm by March 15 or lose the reservation. You may submit only one application; duplicates bring a three-year restriction.

items.t: Before and after the control season
items.d: Dates outside May 28 to September 3 are not in the lottery. They open for first-come reservation on October 1 at 8 a.m. Mountain.

A camp request form is emailed 14 days before launch. List every person, the trip length and the fees on Recreation.gov no later than 7 days before launch. Camps are assigned from your request and are final once the permit is issued.

The River Clerk emails the permit 5 or 6 days before launch. Print and sign it and carry it for the whole trip. A reservation is not the permit and does not guarantee passage: fire, debris flows and logjams can block the river or the access roads.
The date you first enter the permitted stretch is your launch date, even if you start from a tributary or fly in. It cannot be adjusted.
For cancellation pick-ups within 14 days of launch, contact the River Office right away.
May 28 to September 3. A permit is required all year, between Dagger Falls and the Main Salmon confluence.
No more than seven float parties, commercial and private combined, launch each day.
1 to 10 people: up to 8 days (7 nights). 11 to 20: up to 7 days (6 nights). 21 to 24: up to 6 days (5 nights).
August 8 to September 15: a maximum of 12 watercraft per permit, to protect spawning Chinook.
The permit holder must be at least 18 on the launch date, must be on the trip, and the permit is not transferable. Alternate trip leaders are not allowed.
Demand is extreme. One report counts nearly 20,000 applicants for about 353 control-season permits in 2025, a chance of under 2 percent.
$6, non-refundable.
$4 per person per day, or a Salmon Rivers Season Pass ($40, covers only the holder).
50 percent off for Senior and Access pass holders. Enter the pass number in the reservation and bring the pass and photo ID.
Recreation fees are refunded for reduced or cancelled trips. No-shows are not refunded.
Cancel at least 21 days before launch, by 11:59 p.m. Mountain, to avoid a late penalty.
Cancel at least 3 days before launch.
If water is above 5.0 ft or the Boundary Creek road is closed within 14 days of launch, or you booked within 21 days, you may cancel 3 days before launch. You must still cancel.
A late cancellation or no-show means no permit and no lottery for three years.
